name: Easy jog
why: Raises your heart rate and body temperature gradually so your muscles and tendons are ready to work.
setup: Start at an easy, conversational pace.
stopIf: Pain that changes the way you run.

name: Leg swings, forward and back
why: Loosens the hips and hamstrings through the range you use when running, without the performance dip of long static stretches.
setup: Stand side-on to a wall, tree or post with one hand on it.
cues: Swing your outside leg forward and back
mistakes: Arching the back on the back swing
stopIf: Sharp pain in the hip or the back of the thigh.

name: Leg swings, side to side
why: Loosens the inner and outer hip muscles that steady you on each stride.
setup: Face a wall, tree or post with both hands on it.
cues: Swing one leg across your body and out

name: Walking lunge with a twist
why: Opens the hip flexors, wakes up the glutes and turns the mid back, all in one warm-up move.
cues: Turn your chest towards the front leg
mistakes: Twisting from the knee instead of the trunk
feel: Hips, thighs and mid back loosening.

name: Open and close the gate
why: Circles the hip through rotation, waking up the joint and the small muscles around it.
setup: Stand tall, holding a wall or post if needed.
cues: Lift your knee up and out to the side
Circle it open, like opening a gate
stopIf: Pinching at the front of the hip.

name: A-skips
why: A running drill that rehearses a quick knee lift and a springy foot strike under your hips.
cues: Land on the ball of the foot, under your hips
mistakes: Reaching the foot out in front
feel: Light, springy effort in the calves and hips.
stopIf: Pain in the calf, Achilles, shin or knee.

name: High knees
why: Quick, light steps with high knees prime the hip flexors and calves for running.
cues: Lift your knees to hip height
Stay tall on the balls of your feet
feel: Light, quick effort in the hips and calves.
stopIf: Pain in the calf, Achilles, shin, knee or hip.

name: Butt kicks
why: Loosens the front of the thighs and rehearses a quick heel recovery under the body.
cues: Flick your heels up behind you
feel: The front of the thighs loosening.

name: Strides
why: Short, relaxed accelerations to near your fast pace prime your legs and running form before a workout or race.
setup: Find 80 to 100 metres of flat ground. Walk back between strides.
cues: Build up over the first half
Tall and relaxed at top speed
feel: Fast but relaxed: not a sprint.
stopIf: Any tug or sharp pain in the calf or hamstring.
cautions: Skip these if a tendon problem flares with speed.
